text:
nina: Heads up — our retro git-leak scan just flagged a commit in the dotfiles repo that contains an exported KMS plaintext snippet from someone's local bash_history. Link: https://github.com/redwood/dotfiles/commit/abcdef123456 :rotating_light:

sam: wait what, bash_history got committed? how old is the commit?

alex: commit is from 2021-10-12, merged via a cleanup PR. The diff shows someone accidentally added a file `config/legacy-creds.yml` with an inline block that looks like a decrypted key.

jules: severity? can that key be used to sign artifacts or access infra? :eyes:

sam: looks like a signing key plaintext (not a short-lived token). High severity until we confirm. alex, can you paste the safe excerpt (no raw key) so we know the pattern?

alex: sure — here's the offending snippet (redacted):
```
# from committed file config/legacy-creds.yml
private_key: "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
MII...REDACTED...QAB
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
service_account: deploy-bot@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

alex: context — dev ran a local gcloud kms decrypt and then accidentally echoed the plaintext into a local config file which later got added to the dotfiles repo during a mass clean. The plaintext persisted in git history.

nina: ok plan suggestion: (1) rotate the KMS key + destroy any current key versions (2) revoke any SA keys for deploy-bot (3) scrub the repo history (git filter-repo or BFG) and force-push, (4) scan forks and mirrors, (5) open incident ticket and customer-impact assessment if any signing was used.

sam: I can take (1) and (2) now. Alex, can you do (3) and coordinate a safe force-push window? Jules, can you own notifications/postmortem?

jules: yep, I’ll draft an incident notice and schedule postmortem. Need timeline and who to notify (security council + platform + releases).

alex: starting scrub locally. command I'll run (no raw values):
```bash
# example filter-repo invocation
git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/dotfiles.git
python3 -m git_filter_repo --path config/legacy-creds.yml --invert-paths
# verify, then force-push
cd dotfiles.git
git push --force --all
```

sam: rotating KMS now — doing controlled rotation and marking the currently exposed key as compromised. Commands: (we'll run with proper auth)
```bash
gcloud kms keys versions destroy 3 --location=global --keyring=prod --key=signing-key
# create new key/version and update signing configs
```

sam: also creating new service-account keys and revoking the old ones. I'll post tickets for rotation in the infra runbook so releases know to pick up new key.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created: "dotfiles: plaintext signing key committed in repo history". Severity: HIGH. Runbook assigned: sec/ci-leaks.

nina: alex — after scrub, please run a full-org grep + repo scan for similar filenames and patterns (legacy-creds.yml, config/*.yml, *.key, .bash_history, history.*). Add these patterns to our denylist in pre-receive hooks.

alex: will do. Also will search forks, org mirrors, and npm/git caches. We should assume the blob could have been cloned.

jules: comms draft in #inc-commms channel — will share a short external-facing blurb for product/pm review. No evidence of customer impact yet. We should prepare for the possibility signing was used to publish a release; infra to check signatures for anomalous activity since 2021-10-12.

sam: quick note — this is why we need ephemeral local decrypt workflows. Adding a follow-up action to require tools to write to /dev/shm by default and forbid writing decrypted secrets to disk in dev docs.

nina: owners recap: sam = rotate keys + revoke SA, alex = scrub + org scan + pre-receive updates, jules = comms + postmortem, nina = incident lead and escalation. Target: contain today, scrub + scans by EOD, full postmortem in 3 business days.

jules: creating the postmortem ticket with action items and due dates. tagging @releases @platform for signature verification.

sec-bot: Note: automated leak-scan rule updated to catch multiline PEM blocks in yaml/json files (rule id: PEM_YAML_2026).

sam: done with SA revocation and KMS rotation — details in secure ticket (internal ref). Will share timeline in the incident ticket, but flagged for immediate rollout to release builds. :white_check_mark:

alex: scrub complete locally, pushing to a maintenance branch for CI run of integration tests before force-push. I'll coordinate a 15-min window for the push to avoid CI churn.

nina: thanks everyone. after force-push, run a global scan and then we'll close the containment phase. Postmortem owners to meet tomorrow. :thumbsup:

jules: noted. I'll publish the initial incident summary after alex confirms force-push success.

sam: one more TODO — update onboarding docs to show example of safe KMS decrypt flow and add pre-commit hook to warn on PEM blocks.

alex: confirmed force-push completed, global scan running. No other identical blobs found so far.

jules: initial summary posted to #inc-commms. moving to containment -> eradication. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-25 10:00 PT.

nina: closing loop: add retention checks for archived backups (S3 snapshots) — ensure we purge any archived copies that contain the secret. Added to postmortem.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 status updated: CONTAINED.

nina: great work team. We'll follow through on the remediation checklist in the postmortem. :sparkles:
